title: Private Deployments — VPC & On-Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document gathers the canonical deployment guidance for Redwood Private: VPC and on-prem packaging, standard reference architectures, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade/rollback playbooks. It also consolidates the Customer Requirements Library (CRL) used by Solutions and Sales to evaluate and scope private deployments. This page is intended for SREs, platform engineers, solutions engineers, and on-call operators.

Scope
- VPC-hosted Private control plane deployments (single-tenant VPC)
- On-prem / air-gapped package and reference architecture for customer datacenters
- Day-2 operational runbooks (backup, scaling, incident triage)
- Upgrade and rollback procedures for both control plane and data plane components
- Customer Requirements Library for presales and deployment scoping

Prerequisites (customer)
- Network: Dedicated VPC or VLAN with documented CIDR blocks, routable to Redwood control plane endpoints or private peering.
- DNS: Customer-managed zones with delegation options; wildcard TLS certs or ACME-enabled cert manager.
- Identity & Keys: KMS/HSM access or customer-managed keys for secrets; LDAP/SSO (SAML/OIDC) for RBAC.
- Hardware/storage: For on-prem, minimum node specs and storage IOPS targets (see Reference Architecture).
- Compliance: Required audits, data residency requirements, and approved network/security exception forms.

Reference architectures
1) VPC Single-AZ (pilot)
- Use case: Proof-of-concept or low-throughput customers.
- Components: 3 control-plane instances (HA), 2 model-serving nodes (GPU or CPU), PostgreSQL RDS-style managed DB, S3-compatible object store for artifacts.
- Network: Private subnets for nodes, NAT for egress, security groups locked to Redwood-managed CIDRs.
- Sizing guidance: start with 1 x p4d-equivalent model server for 1-5 RPS generation workload.

2) VPC Multi-AZ (production)
- Use case: SLA-backed production workloads.
- Components: Multi-AZ control plane (3+ instances), autoscaling model pools (GPU- and CPU-backed pools), managed DB with cross-AZ replication, multi-AZ object store, cross-AZ load balancer with health checks.
- Availability: target 99.95% control-plane availability, model serving SLOs defined per pool.
- Notes: Cross-AZ placement policies and graceful draining are required to meet SLOs.

3) On-Prem High-Density (regulated environments)
- Use case: Air-gapped or sensitive workloads requiring on-prem hardware.
- Components: Kubernetes cluster (K8s 1.26+ recommended) or bare-metal orchestration with our packaging layer, dedicated GPU nodes, separate management network, on-prem object store (MinIO/CEPH), customer-managed Postgres or supported HA DB cluster.
- Security: Strict network segmentation, on-prem KMS/HSM integration, FIPS-mode options where required.
- Storage: SSD-backed NVMe for model cache, NFS/CEPH for shared volumes with >=10k IOPS for model artifacts.

On-Prem Packaging and Distribution
- Package format: tarball + installer binary (.run) for air-gapped installs; Helm charts for K8s-enabled sites.
- Installer capabilities: offline dependency installation, certificate bundle injection, CI-validated package signature verification.
- Example install flow (air-gapped):
  1. Provide customer with signed package and offline bundle.
  2. Customer uploads bundle to staging host within air-gapped network.
  3. Run installer: sudo ./redwood-private-installer.run --config /opt/redwood/config.yaml --offline-bundle /opt/redwood/bundle.tar.gz
  4. Installer validates signatures, unpacks artifacts, applies systemd/K8s manifests, and performs health checks.
- Configuration: All runtime configuration is delivered as YAML. See Appendix for example config snippets.

Network and Security Configuration
- Minimum egress & ingress rules: only allow required ports between subnets (HTTP/HTTPS for control plane, gRPC/TCP for model-serving, etc.).
- TLS: Mutual TLS for all internal service-to-service traffic in on-prem deployments. TLS certificates must be centrally managed and rotated at least every 90 days.
- Secrets: Integrate with customer KMS; Redwood supports AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault, and HSM appliances (PKCS#11).

Day-2 Operations (runbooks)
1) Routine checks (daily)
- Verify control-plane health: curl -f https://control-plane.local/healthz (expect 200)
- Check model-serving pool utilization: redwoodctl pools list && redwoodctl pools metrics --last 1h
- Disk and cache: df -h /var/lib/redwood && check KV cache hit ratios in Console.

2) Backups and restores
- DB backup cadence: nightly logical backups plus continuous WAL shipping for DBs supporting point-in-time recovery.
- Object-store snapshot: daily incrementals + weekly full snapshots to an immutable archive location.
- Restore test: quarterly restore verification where we restore a copy of DB and object-store to a staging cluster and run smoke tests.

3) Scaling events
- Autoscaling: configured via target CPU/GPU utilization and queue latency. For manual scale-out: redwoodctl scale --pool model-gpu --replicas 6
- Warm-up: when adding GPU nodes, preload model shards and warm KV caches before routing production traffic.

4) Troubleshooting common incidents
- Symptom: Increased latency for short requests
  - Check: model-serving queue length, CPU/GPU utilization, network latency to DB/cache.
  - Remediation: temporarily scale model-serving pool, increase batching timeout for low-priority routes, enable degraded-mode routing to smaller model variant.
- Symptom: Control plane degraded (503s)
  - Check: control-plane logs, DB connectivity, leader election status.
  - Remediation: restart control-plane pod(s) with graceful shutdown, failover DB if necessary, engage on-call SRE.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures
Principles:
- All upgrades must be tested in a staging environment that mirrors production (configuration and data volume).
- Use canary-style rollouts for control-plane and serving runtime.
- Maintain a tested rollback artifact and procedure before making changes.

Control-plane upgrade (recommended flow)
1. Create a release candidate in staging and run full integration smoke tests.
2. Tag the release and create automated migration plan (DB migrations explicit, backwards compatible).
3. Canaries: deploy to 10% of control-plane instances (or to a dedicated canary AZ) and monitor for 30 minutes for errors, latency regressions, and failed migrations.
4. Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15-30 minute observation windows and automated health checks.
5. Post-upgrade: run post-migration verification tasks (background job queues, metrics baseline checks).

Rollback steps (control-plane)
- If canary fails, immediately rollback to previous tag for canary instances and halt rollout.
- If full rollout has issues and DB migrations are irreversible, execute emergency mitigation (feature flags to disable incompatible features) and open an incident.
- Formal rollback command (example): redwoodctl release rollback --component control-plane --to-tag vX.Y.Z --verify

Model-serving runtime upgrade
- Rolling restart by pool with version pinning. For GPU pools, drain traffic from nodes before restart and ensure model shards are reloaded on new version.
- Use version compatibility matrix to ensure new runtime accepts existing cached KV formats.

Emergency rollback (on-prem air-gapped)
- Keep previous installer package and image bundle on staging host for expedited redeploy.
- Restore DB from last known good snapshot if runtime state is incompatible.

Change windows and maintenance policies
- Default maintenance window: Sat 02:00-06:00 local timezone for production upgrades (negotiable with customer).
- Emergency changes can be performed outside the window with approval from the customer security owner and Redwood on-call.

Customer Requirements Library (CRL)
The CRL below enumerates common requirements and the Redwood response or design pattern for each. Use this table to rapidly answer presales questions and to seed the deployment runbook.
Requirement | Typical Customer Ask | Redwood Response / Implementation
--- | --- | ---
Network segmentation | "We need all traffic restricted to our internal subnets" | Deployment into customer VPC with private subnets, strict SGs, and optional private peering.
TLS and certs | "We require customer-managed TLS certs" | Installer accepts PKCS#12 bundles or integrates with on-prem ACME/CertManager; supports external cert rotation.
Data residency | "Data must remain in-country" | Deploy control plane and data plane within customer-selected region or on-prem location; object-store and DB hosted locally.
KMS/HSM | "Keys must be in our HSM" | Support for PKCS#11 HSMs and HashiCorp Vault with transit secrets engine; integration patterns documented.
Auditing & logs | "We need immutable audit logs" | Ship logs to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) and immutable archive for 365+ days if required.
SLA & availability | "We require 99.9%+ SLA" | Multi-AZ deployment with autoscaling and active health checks; recommended capacity commitments and Dedicated plan.
Air-gapped install | "We are fully air-gapped" | Provide signed offline bundle, on-site installation support, and verified checksum/signed packages.
Backup and retention | "We need 7 years retention for backups" | Support long-term archive to customer object store with lifecycle policies; restore SLAs vary by retention class.
Third-party integrations | "Integrate with customer LDAP / SSO" | Provide SAML/OIDC connectors and LDAP sync; RBAC mapping guidelines included.

How to use the CRL
1. During discovery, map each customer requirement to a CRL row and mark custom items for engineering review.
2. For items marked "requires engineering", create a ticket in the Private Deployments backlog with customer context and target delivery date.
3. Maintain a per-customer risk register for deviations from reference architecture.

Appendix: Example Configs
- Minimal control-plane YAML snippet:```yaml
control_plane:
  replicas: 3
  tls:
    mode: mTLS
    cert_source: external
  db:
    type: postgres
    host: db.internal.local
    port: 5432
```

- Model pool example (GPU pool):```yaml
model_pools:
  - name: gpu-large
    node_type: p4d.24xlarge
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 10
    batching:
      max_tokens: 4096
      max_latency_ms: 30
```
